evidence.title: Loreta Janeta Velázquez
evidence.text: Loreta Janeta Velázquez (June 26, 1842 – 1923), was a Cuban-born woman who masqueraded as a male Confederate soldier during the American Civil War.

evidence.title: Loreta Janeta Velázquez
evidence.text: After her soldier husband's accidental death, she enlisted in the Confederate States Army in 1861.

evidence.title: Loreta Janeta Velázquez
evidence.text: She then fought at Bull Run, Ball's Bluff, and Fort Donelson, but was discharged when her gender was discovered while in New Orleans.

evidence.title: Loreta Janeta Velázquez
evidence.text: Undeterred, she reenlisted and fought at Shiloh, until unmasked once more.

evidence.title: Loreta Janeta Velázquez
evidence.text: She then became a Confederate spy, working in both male and female guises, and as a double agent also reporting to the U.S. Secret Service.

evidence.title: Loreta Janeta Velázquez
evidence.text: She remarried three more times, being widowed in each instance.

evidence.title: Loreta Janeta Velázquez
evidence.text: According to William C Davis, she died in January 1923 under the name Loretta J. Beard after many years away from the public eye in a public psychiatric facility, St. Elizabeths Hospital.

evidence.title: Loreta Janeta Velázquez
evidence.text: She spied on the Union for about 5 years.

evidence.title: St. Elizabeths Hospital
evidence.text: St. Elizabeths Hospital opened in 1855 as the first federally operated psychiatric hospital in the United States.

evidence.title: St. Elizabeths Hospital
evidence.text: Housing over 8,000 patients at its peak in the 1950s, the hospital at one point had a fully functioning medical-surgical unit, a school of nursing, and accredited internships and psychiatric residencies.

evidence.title: St. Elizabeths Hospital
evidence.text: Its campus was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1990.

evidence.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
evidence.text: Vassar Brother Medical Center (locally known as Vassar Hospital or VBMC) is a major medical facility located in the city of Poughkeepsie, New York that is a member of the Health Quest network, a nonprofit family of hospitals and healthcare centers in the Hudson Valley area.

evidence.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
evidence.text: VBMC is one of two major medical centers located in Dutchess County, New York, the other being Mid-Hudson Regional Hospital of Westchester Medical Center.

evidence.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
evidence.text: The hospital was first incorporated in 1882 under the name Vassar Brothers Hospital, following contributions made by John Guy Vassar following the death of his brother.

evidence.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
evidence.text: The hospital opened its doors in 1887, and initially had 40 beds divided up into four wards, each containing ten beds.

evidence.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
evidence.text: At the time the hospital opened it also contained a labor and delivery ward, a children's ward, a nursery, three private rooms, and two isolation rooms.

evidence.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
evidence.text: Several major renovations occurred in 1983, 1991, and 2001; adding critical care areas, a new operating and delivery wing, and a cancer care center, respectively.

evidence.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
evidence.text: In 2002 Vassar Brothers Hospital officially became Vassar Brothers Medical Center.

evidence.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
evidence.text: In September 2016, VBMC announced a new $500 million expansion which would almost double the number of available rooms.

evidence.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
evidence.text: Construction on the expansion is expected to be completed in 2019.
